hints.title: Buyer Brand Adoption Filtering
hints.text: Identify customers who purchased an S8 model while having never purchased an iPhone model.

hints.title: Conditional Sum Group Constraints
hints.text: Join sales to products, group by buyer identifier, and enforce positive presence for S8 and zero presence for iPhone.

hints.title: Brand Analysis Query Blueprint
hints.text: select s.buyer_id from Sales s join Product p on s.product_id = p.product_id group by s.buyer_id having sum(case when p.product_name = "S8" then 1 else 0 end) > 0 and sum(case when p.product_name = "iPhone" then 1 else 0 end) = 0.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT s.buyer_id
FROM Sales s
JOIN Product p ON s.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY s.buyer_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN p.product_name = 'S8' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN p.product_name = 'iPhone' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0;
```

variables: P: number of product catalog entries
complexity.notes: Equi-join on product identifier followed by single-pass hash aggregation runs in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simple where clause filters out rows rather than checking buyer purchase history in aggregate.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouped conditional sum avoids two separate distinct subqueries and anti-joins.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of conditional aggregation in HAVING clause or EXCEPT / NOT IN pattern.

solutions.approach: Grouped Conditional Aggregation on Product Names

solutions.code:
SELECT s.buyer_id
FROM Sales s
JOIN Product p ON s.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY s.buyer_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN p.product_name = 'S8' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN p.product_name = 'iPhone' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0;

import pandas as pd

def sales_analysis(product: pd.DataFrame, sales: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = sales.merge(product, on='product_id')
    grouped = df.groupby('buyer_id')['product_name'].agg(set).reset_index()
    res = grouped[grouped['product_name'].apply(lambda x: 'S8' in x and 'iPhone' not in x)]
    return res[['buyer_id']]
